change_note: Each card gains a plain one-sentence summary with no numbers, for the simple home page and the one-stock brief; the research itself is unchanged.
purpose: What's next for each company on our list: its latest quarter, what it says about the coming one, when it next reports and what is coming up. Context for the household, researched from the companies' own releases and filings.
how_to_read: What a company says about its future is its own statement, not a forecast we endorse.
We paraphrase in our own words and link to the source; we never copy their text.
No prices, price targets or analyst ratings, ever: only what the company reported and announced.
Cards are refreshed after each earnings season; each one shows the day it was researched.
A card is flagged when new results are out, or probably out, since it was written, until it is refreshed.
The plain summary is one sentence with no numbers, written from the same card for a quick read.

companies.name: Apple Inc.
companies.business: Sells iPhone, Mac, iPad, wearables (Watch, AirPods) and services such as the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple Pay and advertising.
companies.plain: Apple: iPhone and Mac sales grew strongly; its first foldable iPhone goes on sale later this month, but chip and memory shortages could hurt sales and profit.

highlights: iPhone $54.3B (+22%, led by Pro models), Mac $10.4B (+29%), Services $30.7B (+12%); iPad down 6%; Greater China +22%.
Gross margin 50.1% (46.5% a year earlier), helped by product mix and tariff refunds; profit per share $2.02, up 29%.
Bought back $25.8B of stock and paid $4.0B dividends in the quarter; a new $100B buyback program was added in April 2026.

guidance.text: Gives its outlook only on the earnings call; we found no written copy from the company to link.

next_earnings.note: Expected; not yet confirmed on Apple's own investor site.

whats_next.item: iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable iPhone (from $1,999 in the US): pre-orders 16 Oct, on sale 23 Oct in 70+ countries, 28 more on 30 Oct.
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (A20 Pro chip, 2nm) launched: pre-orders 12 Sep, in stores 18 Sep, 20 more countries 25 Sep.
whats_next.when: September 2026 (first weeks fall in fiscal Q4)

whats_next.item: Siri AI launched in beta with iOS 27 (English first); French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish to follow; not initially in the EU.
whats_next.when: iOS 27 on 14 Sep 2026; more languages in October 2026

whats_next.item: CEO change: John Ternus became CEO and Tim Cook Executive Chair on 1 Sep 2026.

watch.item: Apple says chip, memory (DRAM) and storage (NAND) shortages and cost increases are expected to intensify and could hurt revenue and margins.
Tariffs: refunds after a 20 Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling lifted Q3 margin, but further Section 232/301 or other tariff measures remain possible.
Legal: US DOJ antitrust suit over smartphones, EU Digital Markets Act probes and Epic Games App Store case remain open.

companies.name: Microsoft Corporation
companies.business: Sells cloud computing (Azure), Microsoft 365/Copilot and other business software, LinkedIn, Windows, Xbox gaming and search advertising.
companies.plain: Microsoft: its cloud business is growing fast and it keeps spending heavily on data centers; Windows and Xbox sales fell.

highlights: Microsoft Cloud revenue $59.3B (+27%); Azure and other cloud services +43%; Azure passed $100B annual revenue; Microsoft 365 Copilot over 30M paid seats.
Operating income $40.6B (+18%); net income $35.8B (+31%), helped by a $3.2B gain on its Anthropic investment.
Commercial remaining performance obligation up 84% to $678B; $10.2B returned to shareholders in the quarter.

guidance.text: Revenue $89.85B-$90.95B; Azure growth 44%-45% in constant currency (new Azure definition); operating margin roughly flat from a year earlier; capital spending over $50B in the quarter.

next_earnings.note: Expected: Microsoft's investor events page lists Wednesday 28 Oct 2026 for FY27 Q1; no formal date press release or call time seen yet.

whats_next.item: New reporting from FY27: two segments, Agents and Infra (Azure, Microsoft 365, GitHub) and Devices and Consumer (search/ads, Xbox, Windows), with restated history.
Continued heavy data-center build: FY26 additions to property and equipment were $115.9B, up from $64.6B in FY25.
whats_next.when: fiscal 2026; over $50B planned for Q1 fiscal 2027

whats_next.item: Microsoft guided Microsoft 365 commercial cloud growth of about 17% in constant currency for Q1 FY27 under the new definition (now including GitHub).

watch.item: OpenAI ties: about 25% stake; FY26 revenue from OpenAI arrangements $24.1B; its adjusted results leave out swings in the OpenAI investment's value.
10-K flags power availability and limited datacenter component supply as possible limits on capacity growth.
Consumer side weak in Q4: More Personal Computing revenue -4%, Windows OEM/Devices -7%, Xbox content and services -10%.

companies.name: NVIDIA Corporation
companies.business: Designs AI accelerators (GPUs), CPUs, networking gear and full rack-scale AI data-center systems with software, plus PC/workstation graphics and robotics/auto chips.
companies.plain: Nvidia: sales of its AI chips are still growing very fast and its next chips have started shipping, but it says it is mostly shut out of China.

highlights: Data Center revenue $89.0B, up 117% from a year earlier and 18% from last quarter; largest cloud companies $48.7B (+102%), other AI clouds, industry and enterprise $40.3B (+138%).
Gross margin 75.0%; net income $59.7B (+126%); Edge Computing (PCs, workstations, robotics) revenue $7.2B, up 27% from a year earlier.
Returned about $26.0B in Q2 via buybacks and dividends; supply commitments rose to $279B from $119B, mainly for memory.

guidance.text: Revenue about $108.0B (within 2% either way), assuming no China data-center compute revenue; gross margin about 74.0% (within half a point either way); operating expenses about $9.2B.

next_earnings.note: Not yet announced by NVIDIA as of 8 Oct 2026; in recent years the Q3 report came on a Wednesday in the second half of November, with the date set in late October.

whats_next.item: Vera Rubin, the platform after Blackwell, began production shipments; NVIDIA says it will ship Blackwell and Rubin side by side and faces some supply limits.

Rubin Ultra will add NVIDIA's new Kyber rack with 144 GPUs as a standalone option, next to 72- and 576-GPU setups; NVIDIA says Kyber will later scale to 1,152 GPUs as the base for Feynman, the architecture after Rubin.
whats_next.when: not dated in the linked post

whats_next.item: Agreed on 2 Sep 2026 to buy Hugging Face (open-model platform) for about $11.9B plus up to ~$1.0B retention equity, pending regulatory approvals.
whats_next.when: expected to close in first half of 2027

whats_next.item: Backing a ~4.25 GW AI campus in Ohio (SB Energy, OpenAI as tenant) with guarantees capped at $105B; NVIDIA says each GPU generation there could mean $150-200B revenue.

watch.item: Export controls: Beijing has limited US-licensed H200 sales; H200 shipments under 1% of Data Center revenue after a $0.4B H200 charge; NVIDIA says it is effectively shut out of China data centers.
Rising commitments: $366B in supply, cloud, lease and other commitments plus up to $108.5B in data-center guarantees, $105B of it tied to the Ohio campus leased to OpenAI.
Receivables climbed to $63.1B (60 days of sales, from 45) due to longer payment terms on large multi-quarter deals.

companies.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
companies.business: Online retail and third-party marketplace, Amazon Web Services cloud computing, advertising, and Prime subscriptions.
companies.plain: Amazon: its cloud arm grew at its fastest pace in years, but heavy spending, mostly for AI, meant more cash went out than came in over the past year.

highlights: AWS sales rose 37% to $42.2B, its fastest growth in 18 quarters. AWS operating income was $16.6B, up from $10.2B a year earlier.
Operating income rose to $27.5B from $19.2B. Net income of $62.6B includes $53.4B of pre-tax non-operating income, mainly from its Anthropic investments.
Trailing-12-month free cash flow was an outflow of $7.6B, versus an inflow of $18.2B a year earlier, after net equipment purchases rose $66.1B, mostly for AI.

guidance.text: Expects Q3 net sales of $197B-$202B (+9% to 12%; nearly 4 points higher excluding Prime Day in both years) and operating income of $22.5B-$26.5B, versus $17.4B a year earlier.

next_earnings.note: As of 2026-10-08 Amazon has not announced its Q3 2026 date. It announced the Q2 call about two weeks ahead (16 Jul for 30 Jul), and has reported Q3 in late October in past years.

whats_next.item: Amazon Leo satellite internet: nearly 400 satellites in orbit, which Amazon says is enough to start initial service.
whats_next.when: this year (2026), per the Q2 release

whats_next.item: Pending acquisition of Globalstar (satellite operator) for cash and Amazon stock, with cash limited to 40% of Globalstar shares; Amazon and Globalstar expect it to close in 2027.
About $496B of contracted services not yet booked as revenue, mostly AWS. In 2026, OpenAI expanded its AWS commitment by $100B and Anthropic by more than $100B.
whats_next.when: multi-year (avg. remaining life 6.4 years, as of 30 Jun 2026)

whats_next.item: Zoox received an NHTSA exemption allowing it to charge for robotaxi rides. Alexa+ expanded to Germany, Austria, France and Brazil.
whats_next.when: no launch date given for paid Zoox service

watch.item: Issued £4.25B of sterling senior notes in four tranches (due 2029-2045) on 14 Sept 2026, at a time when trailing free cash flow was negative.
Headline profit relies on non-operating gains from its Anthropic stake, which can swing either way from quarter to quarter.
Antitrust and consumer-protection cases from the FTC, state attorneys general and private plaintiffs in the US, Canada and UK seek billions in damages.

companies.name: Alphabet Inc.
companies.business: Google Search and advertising, YouTube, Google Cloud (including Gemini AI models and TPU chips), Android and devices, plus other ventures.
companies.plain: Alphabet: its cloud business is growing very fast and search keeps growing; it borrowed and sold new shares, and two big court cases over its market power are open.

highlights: Google Cloud revenue rose 82% to $24.8B and its operating income rose to $8.8B from $2.8B. Search and other revenue grew 17% to $63.3B.
Operating income rose 30% to $40.8B (34% margin). Profit per share of $9.11 includes a $99.0B gain on equity securities, which added $6.26 per share.
Capital spending was $44.9B and quarterly free cash flow was negative $5.9B. No buybacks. Raised $49.6B net from stock issuance and $20.3B from notes.

guidance.text: The company gives no outlook for the coming period.

next_earnings.note: Q3 2026 call on Wed 28 Oct 2026, 1:30pm PT / 4:30pm ET. Alphabet announced the date on 6 Oct 2026.

whats_next.item: Revenue backlog of $519.5B, of which $513.9B is Google Cloud. Alphabet expects to recognize just over half of it within 24 months.
whats_next.when: next 24 months and beyond (as of 30 Jun 2026)

whats_next.item: Closed a $25B US dollar senior notes offering in ten tranches, maturing 2028 to 2056 and beyond, after the Q2 stock and note raises.
The Gemini app has 950M monthly users and nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 use Gemini Enterprise. Alphabet also introduced Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber alongside its security products.
$69.5B remains under the $70B buyback authorization from Apr 2025, but no shares were repurchased in H1 2026. A $0.22 quarterly dividend was paid 14 Sep 2026.
whats_next.when: no expiration date on the program

watch.item: Ad-tech antitrust case: the final remedies judgment is still pending after Nov 2025 closing arguments. Google says DOJ's structural remedies could be materially adverse.
Search antitrust case: Google (Jan 2026) and the DOJ and states (Feb 2026) both appealed the final judgment, which requires data-sharing and syndication to rivals.
Large gains on equity holdings drove Q2 profit per share. Alphabet says swings in these investments could make other income significantly volatile in future periods.

companies.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
companies.business: Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, funded by advertising, plus Reality Labs (AI glasses, VR headsets) and Meta AI.
companies.plain: Meta: ad sales grew strongly, but costs grew even faster and profit fell; new AI glasses ship this month, and more child-safety court cases start soon.

highlights: Ad impressions rose 14% and average price per ad rose 12%. Daily active people across its apps reached 3.60B (+3%).
Costs rose 55% to $42.0B, including a $2.4B legal charge and $1.18B of severance from the May 2026 layoffs. Operating margin fell to 31% from 43%, and net income fell 14% to $15.85B.
Family of Apps operating income was $23.4B and Reality Labs lost $4.6B. Capital spending, including finance-lease principal, was $31.1B. No buybacks.

guidance.text: Q3 revenue of $61-64B. For FY2026: total expenses of $165-169B, capital spending of $130-145B (narrowed from $125-145B), and operating income above 2025's level.

next_earnings.note: As of 2026-10-08 Meta has not announced its Q3 2026 date; its 2026 IR announcement page does not exist yet. Meta reported Q3 2025 on 29 Oct 2025. Third-party calendars estimate 28 Oct 2026, which Meta has not confirmed.

whats_next.item: Meta VR Glasses, a roughly 100-gram VR headset in a glasses frame, tethered to a pocket puck that holds compute and battery. Price $1,299.99.
New AI glasses: Ray-Ban Meta Audio from $349, and a new Meta Adventurer version from $249. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 is on sale from $449.
whats_next.when: Audio ships 13 Oct 2026; Adventurer on sale 23 Oct 2026

whats_next.item: Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, is coming to its AI glasses. A US hearing-enhancement feature ($149.99, or included with Meta One) is also launching.
whats_next.when: Muse in the coming months; hearing feature later in 2026

whats_next.item: Full-year 2026 capital spending planned at $130-145B to support AI and the core business. Meta issued $25B of senior notes in May 2026.

watch.item: US youth-safety litigation: juries ruled against Meta in two trials (a $375M New Mexico penalty and a $6M award shared with YouTube). The next two user bellwether trials start 28 Oct 2026.
EU Commission issued preliminary Digital Services Act findings (Apr and Jul 2026) on under-13 users and potentially addictive design on Facebook and Instagram.
In Q2, expenses grew 55% while revenue grew 28%, and operating margin fell to 31% from 43%.

companies.name: Broadcom Inc.
companies.business: Makes custom AI chips (XPUs) and networking chips for big cloud/AI customers, plus broadband, wireless and storage chips; also sells infrastructure software (VMware).
companies.plain: Broadcom: sales of its AI chips more than tripled and it expects even more next quarter; a few big customers bring in over half of its sales.

highlights: AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B, up 221% from a year earlier and 54% from last quarter; semiconductor solutions $20.8B (+127%), infrastructure software $8.8B (+29%).
Net income $13.1B (+216%); adjusted operating income $20.1B (+92%); free cash flow $13.7B, 46% of revenue.
Quarterly dividend held at $0.65/share; cash and equivalents $24.0B at quarter end.

guidance.text: Revenue about $34.8B (+93% from a year earlier), with AI semiconductor revenue expected near $21.7B (+236%); adjusted operating income about 66% of revenue.

next_earnings.note: Not yet announced as of 8 Oct 2026; Broadcom has typically posted its Q4 date in November and reported in mid-December.

whats_next.item: Firm contract backlog of about $179.2B (incl. a long-term custom AI accelerator deal signed last quarter); about 25% expected to become revenue within 12 months.
AI XPV platform with financial partners aims to enable over 20 GW of compute on Broadcom custom XPUs and networking for frontier AI labs; first tranche $35B.
Q4 AI semiconductor revenue expected to accelerate to about $21.7B.
About $10.1B remained available under stock buyback authorizations at quarter end.

watch.item: Customer concentration: top five end customers about 55% of Q3 revenue; direct sales to one distributor alone 50%.
Broadcom backstops a customer's 5-year AI-rack lease obligations; maximum exposure about $29B once all racks deploy (nothing paid so far).
Higher mix of chip sales (lower margin than software) and new rack/lease business models could weigh on gross margin, per the 10-Q.

companies.name: Costco Wholesale Corporation
companies.business: Membership warehouse clubs selling groceries, household goods, gasoline and its Kirkland Signature brand, funded partly by annual membership fees.
companies.plain: Costco: store sales keep growing and online sales grew faster; it plans more new stores this coming year, and it says higher tariffs are more likely to hurt than help.

highlights: Net sales rose 11.2% to $93.9B. Comparable sales rose 9.4% (6.7% excluding gas prices and FX), and digitally-enabled comparable sales rose 19.5%.
Q4 net income was $3.0B ($6.75 per share vs $5.87), including a one-time $0.15 per share benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. Full-year net income was $9.2B.
Q4 membership fees were $1.85B, up from $1.72B. Costco operates 939 warehouses, 647 of them in the US and Puerto Rico.

guidance.text: The company gives no outlook for the coming period.

next_earnings.note: Costco has not announced its Q1 fiscal 2027 date as of 2026-10-08. It usually reports Q1 in December, and third-party calendars estimate about 10 Dec 2026, which Costco has not confirmed.

whats_next.item: Plans to open up to 33 new warehouses, including 5 relocations, after opening 28 (including 3 relocations) in fiscal 2026.
Intends to spend about $7.5B on capital expenditures, up from $6.4B in fiscal 2026.
The $4B buyback authorization from Jan 2023 (about $1.1B left at 30 Aug 2026) expires. The annual shareholder meeting is set for 21 Jan 2027.

watch.item: Costco says higher tariffs are more likely to hurt than help its results. It received $184M of IEEPA refunds in FY2026 and $155M since, mostly for member value.
Four class actions filed in Mar 2026 seek IEEPA tariff refunds for members who paid higher prices. One court denied Costco's motion to dismiss on 17 Jul 2026.

companies.name: Amgen Inc.
companies.business: Biotech drugmaker: heart (Repatha), bone (Prolia, Evenity), inflammation (Tezspire, Tepezza, Uplizna), cancer (Imdelltra, Blincyto) and biosimilars.
companies.plain: Amgen: newer medicines are growing, but copies from other makers are cutting sales of older drugs; a lung cancer drug helped patients live longer in a big trial.

highlights: Product sales grew 9% to $9.5B, mainly on volume. Repatha rose 37% to $953M, Evenity 38%, Tezspire 42%, Imdelltra 115% and Uplizna 90%.
Biosimilar launches cut Prolia sales by 32% and Xgeva by 34%. Adjusted operating margin was 48.4% of product sales, 0.5 points lower than a year earlier.
Free cash flow was $3.5B, up from $1.9B. Amgen bought back no shares in the quarter. The dividend was $2.52 a share, 6% higher than a year earlier.

guidance.text: Total revenues of $38.2B-$39.4B and adjusted profit per share of $22.30-$23.50. Capital spending of about $2.6B. Share buybacks of no more than $3.0B.

next_earnings.note: As of 8 Oct 2026 Amgen had not announced a Q3 2026 date. Amgen usually posts a webcast notice about a week before it reports.

whats_next.item: In the Phase 3 DeLLphi-305 trial, adding Imdelltra to Imfinzi improved overall survival as first-line maintenance in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. Amgen plans to share the data with regulators.
whats_next.when: announced 8 Sep 2026; full data at a coming congress

whats_next.item: Dazodalibep met its main goal in the Phase 3 OASIZ 301 trial in Sjogren's disease. A second Phase 3 trial, OASIZ 303, is still running.
whats_next.when: OASIZ 301 out 22 Sep 2026; OASIZ 303 due Q4 2026

whats_next.item: MariTide, Amgen's obesity drug, is in several MARITIME Phase 3 studies. Three more Phase 3 studies in type 2 diabetes are planned. No readout date given.
whats_next.when: Diabetes studies expected to start in 2026

whats_next.item: The FDA cut required patient monitoring after each of the first two Imdelltra doses from 22-24 hours to 6-8 hours.

watch.item: Biosimilar competition is eating into Prolia and Xgeva. In Q2, Prolia sales fell 32% and Xgeva 34%.
The FDA wants Tavneos off the U.S. market. Amgen asked for a hearing on 1 Jun 2026 and filed supporting materials on 23 Jul 2026. No outcome found as of 8 Oct.
An FDA partial clinical hold stopped new enrollment in two subcutaneous blinatumomab studies. Amgen is talking with the FDA about reopening them.

companies.name: Intuitive Surgical, Inc.
companies.business: Makes da Vinci surgical robots and the Ion lung-biopsy system, plus the instruments, accessories and service that go with them.
companies.plain: Intuitive Surgical: more operations are done with its robots and it placed more of them; it expects to keep a bit more of each sale, while tariffs and rivals are risks.

highlights: Worldwide procedures grew about 16%: da Vinci about 15% and Ion about 36%. Intuitive placed 468 da Vinci systems (246 da Vinci 5), up from 395 a year earlier.
Instruments and accessories revenue rose 18% to $1.73B. Adjusted gross margin was 70.0%, up from 67.9%, helped by IEEPA tariff refunds worth about $0.08 a share.
Cash and investments ended the quarter at $8.63B. Intuitive bought back about 0.9M shares for $0.38B.

guidance.text: da Vinci procedure growth of about 13.5%-15.5%, now expected near the midpoint (same range as April). Adjusted gross margin raised to 68%-69% (was 67.5%-68.5%), including about 1 point of tariff drag. Operating expense growth narrowed to 11%-13% from 11%-14%.

next_earnings.note: Intuitive had not confirmed a Q3 2026 results date on its own site as of 8 Oct 2026.

whats_next.item: In March 2026 the FDA cleared updated da Vinci 5 force-feedback instruments, which can now be used more times. Wider availability depends on making more of them.
whats_next.when: As manufacturing volumes increase (no date given)

whats_next.item: The FDA cleared da Vinci 5 for some chest-access heart procedures, such as mitral valve repair, using instruments without force feedback.
Intuitive bought its distributors in Italy, Spain and Portugal for about $533M and now sells directly in those markets and nearby territories.
whats_next.when: Closed 1 Mar 2026. Shift to direct sales under way.

watch.item: Tariffs: the amount and timing of further IEEPA tariff refunds is uncertain. German-made endoscopes are tariffed, while most Mexico-made instruments are exempt under USMCA.
Intuitive lists competition as a risk, including domestic robot makers in markets such as China.

companies.name: Gilead Sciences, Inc.
companies.business: Biopharma focused on HIV treatment and prevention (Biktarvy, Descovy, Yeztugo), liver disease (Livdelzi), and cancer (Trodelvy, Kite cell therapies).
companies.plain: Gilead: HIV medicines keep growing, but costs of buying other companies led to a loss; a US decision on a new blood cancer treatment is due in December.

highlights: HIV sales grew 12% to $5.7B. Biktarvy rose 7% to $3.8B, Descovy 48% to $967M, and Yeztugo (twice-yearly PrEP) brought in $232M. Trodelvy grew 26% to $457M.
Net loss of $8.45 a share, including $9.08 a share of charges for acquired research and development, $7.0B of it for Arcellx. Cell therapy sales fell 14% to $417M.
Operating cash flow was $3.6B. Gilead paid $1.0B in dividends and bought back $355M of stock. Cash and securities fell to $3.2B after acquisitions and debt repayment.

guidance.text: Product sales of $30.1B-$30.4B. Excluding Veklury, raised to $29.8B-$30.1B (was $29.4B-$29.8B). Veklury cut to about $300M (was about $600M). Adjusted loss of $0.30-$0.65 a share, narrowed from a loss of $0.65-$1.05.

next_earnings.note: As of 8 Oct 2026 Gilead had not announced a Q3 2026 date. Data sites give conflicting estimates (22 Oct or 29 Oct), so no date is shown.

whats_next.item: FDA decision on anito-cel, a therapy made from the patient's own immune cells, for multiple myeloma that has relapsed after three or more prior treatments. Gilead bought partner Arcellx in April 2026.
The FDA approved Bixlenvo (bictegravir + lenacapavir), a once-daily pill that can replace current treatment for adults whose HIV is already suppressed.
whats_next.when: Approved 27 Aug 2026, the FDA's decision date

whats_next.item: The FDA is reviewing a once-weekly Yeztugo pill for HIV prevention.
Islatravir + lenacapavir, a once-weekly HIV treatment pill developed with Merck, had positive results in the Phase 3 ISLEND-1 and ISLEND-2 trials. No filing timing given.

watch.item: Cell therapy sales are falling: in Q2, Yescarta fell 12% and Tecartus 24%. Expected Veklury sales were cut in half, to about $300M.
Cash and securities fell from $10.6B to $3.2B in the first half, after deals (Arcellx, Tubulis, Ouro) and debt repayment. Gilead expects a 2026 loss per share, reported and adjusted.

companies.name: PepsiCo, Inc.
companies.business: Global snacks and drinks: Frito-Lay, Quaker, Pepsi, Gatorade and others, sold through North American and international divisions.
companies.plain: PepsiCo: sales grew slowly, with the growth coming from outside North America, and it lowered its profit outlook for the year; it plans more cost cuts.

highlights: Organic revenue rose 3.1%, with volume growth in both drinks and foods. Core profit per share rose 2% to $2.34. Tariff refunds added about 4 points to core operating profit.
North America foods and beverages were both flat on an organic basis. Abroad, organic growth was 9% in EMEA, 9% in Asia Pacific Foods and 6% in LatAm Foods.
Reported profit per share rose 17% to $2.23. Net revenue for the year to date was $68.9B, up 6.7%.

guidance.text: Organic revenue about +3% and net revenue about +6%. Core profit-per-share growth cut to +2.5%-3.5% (was the low end of +5%-7%). Cash returned to shareholders unchanged at $8.9B: $7.9B dividends and $1.0B buybacks.

next_earnings.note: Q3 was reported 8 Oct 2026. PepsiCo has not yet announced a date for Q4 and full-year results.

whats_next.item: PepsiCo is lining up more structural cost cuts. They are meant to pay for growth spending and offset rising input costs.
whats_next.when: To be carried out in the coming months

whats_next.item: PepsiCo expanded the multi-year productivity plan it started in 2019 and extended it.
Plan to lift North America results with more innovation, stronger brand building and sharper execution in each sales channel.

watch.item: North America is not growing organically. PFNA was flat, and PBNA's 5% reported growth came mainly from acquisitions made in 2025.
Core profit-per-share growth guidance was cut to +2.5%-3.5% from the low end of +5%-7%. Q3 core operating profit got about a 4-point lift from tariff refunds.

companies.name: Monster Beverage Corporation
companies.business: Makes and sells energy drinks worldwide (Monster Energy plus other energy brands it owns) and a small craft beer, malt beverage and hard seltzer line
companies.plain: Monster: energy drink sales grew fast, especially abroad; its beer and seltzer line keeps shrinking, and it lists higher can costs as a risk.

highlights: Monster Energy Drinks segment sales rose 21.6% to $2.36 billion; Alcohol Brands fell 15.2% to $32.2 million
Sales outside the U.S. grew 34.6% to $1.16 billion, about 46% of the quarter's net sales (about 41% a year earlier)
Gross margin 55.9% vs 55.7% (pricing and mix, partly offset by higher aluminum can and freight-in costs); operating income +17.2% to $740.4 million

guidance.text: The company gives no outlook for the coming period.

next_earnings.note: No Q3 2026 date announced as of 2026-10-08; in past years Monster announced its Q3 date in late October and reported in early November (a pattern, not a schedule)

whats_next.item: About $900 million remained available under existing share buyback authorizations; no shares were bought in Q2 2026
Two-for-one stock split paid as a 100% stock dividend, distributed after the close on 10 Aug 2026 with split-adjusted trading expected from 11 Aug
2026 marketing plan raises spending on social, digital and media platforms and partnerships to back existing drinks and new launches

watch.item: Company lists aluminum can costs, the Midwest Premium and additional U.S. tariffs among risks; higher can costs already weighed on Q2 margin
Alcohol Brands (craft beer, malt beverages, hard seltzer) sales kept shrinking, down 15.2% year over year in Q2

companies.name: American Electric Power Company
companies.business: Regulated electric utility serving customers across 11 U.S. states, with one of the largest U.S. power transmission networks
companies.plain: American Electric Power: big users like data centers signed up for more power, and it raised its profit outlook; its building plan depends on that demand arriving.

highlights: Operating profit per share (AEP's adjusted measure) $1.36 vs $1.43; reported $1.31 vs $2.29, as Q2 2025 included a $480M one-time benefit tied to a FERC tax order
Signed about 6 GW more large-load agreements in Q2, mostly in Texas, taking contracted load growth through 2030 to 69 GW
AEP Texas secured a DOE loan of up to $3.3 billion for nearly 100 transmission projects; AEP's DOE loans now total about $5 billion

guidance.text: Raised 2026 operating profit-per-share range to $6.25-$6.55 (from $6.15-$6.45); reaffirmed 7%-9% annual operating earnings growth through 2030

next_earnings.note: Q3 2026 earnings webcast listed on AEP's investor events page for 28 Oct 2026, 9:00 a.m. ET (re-checked 2026-10-08)

whats_next.item: $78 billion capital plan, plus more than $10 billion of further possible investment (Wyoming fuel cell project, Piketon, Ohio transmission, new generation)
About 13 GW of gas turbine capacity secured for possible deployment, with up to 10 GW more being evaluated
Large-load tariffs approved in five states (Virginia added in Q2), three more state filings pending

watch.item: Plan rests on 69 GW of contracted data-center and industrial load arriving through 2030 and on pending state large-load tariff decisions
Operating earnings fell year over year in Q2, which the CEO tied to the 2025 transmission minority-stake sale and tax timing

companies.name: Xcel Energy Inc.
companies.business: Regulated electric and natural gas utility serving customers in eight Western and Midwestern U.S. states (Minnesota, Colorado, Texas, New Mexico and others)
companies.plain: Xcel Energy: profit rose and it raised its payout to shareholders; regulators decide early next year on a Google data center deal, and a Texas wildfire lawsuit is open.

highlights: Reported and ongoing profit per share both $0.93, up from $0.75, mainly from recovery of electric infrastructure spending, partly offset by higher financing costs
Retail electric sales rose 2.1% (1.5% weather-normalized); quarterly dividend raised to $0.5925 from $0.57
Google will pay all costs of serving a new Minnesota data center under an agreement signed earlier in 2026; company sees about $1.1B of customer benefits if approved

guidance.text: Reaffirmed 2026 ongoing profit per share of $4.04-$4.16; long-term goals of 6%-8%+ a year growth in profit per share and 4%-6% a year in the dividend

next_earnings.note: No Q3 2026 call announced as of 2026-10-08; Xcel has reported Q3 in late October in past years (a pattern, not a schedule)

whats_next.item: Minnesota regulators to decide on the Google data center service agreement and a 1,900 MW clean-energy charge
Rate case decisions still pending: Colorado gas ($123M settlement), New Mexico electric ($90M stipulation), Minnesota gas ($38M settlement)
Forward share sale agreements cover 69.7 million unsettled shares, minimum expected proceeds of $5.2 billion

watch.item: Colorado regulators verbally approved a $157M electric rate increase on 19 Aug 2026, below the $225M settlement; new rates expected from 29 Aug
Smokehouse Creek wildfire (Texas): $503M estimated losses and costs, about $80M of insurance left, Texas Attorney General lawsuit pending
Interest expense projected to rise $240-$250 million in 2026 as the company borrows to fund its build-out

companies.name: Cintas Corporation
companies.business: Rents and cleans work uniforms and supplies facility products (mats, restroom supplies), first aid and safety, and fire protection services for businesses
companies.plain: Cintas: its work uniform and safety business keeps growing and it raised its outlook; US and Canadian regulators are still reviewing its planned purchase of UniFirst.

highlights: Organic growth 8.9%; Uniform Rental & Facility Services revenue $2.29 billion (+9.7%); First Aid & Safety $388.5 million (+16.1%)
Gross margin 51.5% (up 1.2 points); operating margin 23.6% vs 22.7%; profit per share $1.36, or $1.39 excluding UniFirst deal costs
Free cash flow $464.8 million; $544.7 million of buybacks in Q1 and through 22 Sep 2026; $208.8 million quarterly dividend paid 15 Sep

guidance.text: Raised revenue outlook to $12.15-$12.27 billion (from $12.10-$12.25B) and adjusted profit per share to $5.45-$5.54 (from $5.36-$5.50); excludes the pending UniFirst deal and future buybacks

next_earnings.note: Q2 fiscal 2027 date not announced as of 2026-10-08; Cintas reported its fiscal Q2 on 18 Dec 2025 last year and in late December in prior years (a pattern, not a schedule)

whats_next.item: UniFirst acquisition: companies certified substantial compliance with the FTC's second request on 2 Oct and agreed not to close before 11 Dec 2026 unless the FTC ends its review sooner
whats_next.when: Cintas still expects closing before end of calendar 2026

whats_next.item: Canada's Competition Bureau is also reviewing the UniFirst deal; the companies completed their response to its information request on 29 Sep 2026

watch.item: FTC review outcome on UniFirst: guidance excludes the deal, so closing would change the numbers; deal costs already trimmed Q1 profit per share by $0.03
Guidance assumes constant exchange rates, no further buybacks and no significant economic disruption or downturn

companies.name: PACCAR Inc
companies.business: Builds heavy trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF brands, and also sells truck parts and provides truck financing and leasing.
companies.plain: PACCAR: truck deliveries were about flat but its parts business had record sales; it names tariffs, pollution rules and a weaker economy as risks.

latest.revenue: $7.55 billion (net sales and financial services revenues)
highlights: Net income was $752.0M ($1.43 per diluted share), up from $723.8M ($1.37) a year earlier. Global truck deliveries were 38,700, versus 39,300 a year earlier.
PACCAR Parts revenue reached a record $1.75B, with pre-tax income of $417.0M. Financial Services pre-tax income was $124.1M.
Dividends declared were $0.35 per share for the quarter, up from $0.33 a year earlier.

guidance.text: PACCAR estimates 2026 Class 8 retail sales of 230,000-270,000 trucks in the US and Canada, and 290,000-330,000 registrations of trucks above 16 tonnes in Europe. It plans $700-750M of capital spending and $450-480M of research and development.

next_earnings.note: PACCAR had not announced a Q3 2026 date as of 8 Oct 2026. Its Q3 2025 results came out on 21 Oct 2025, but that is a past pattern, not a schedule.

whats_next.item: The company says it keeps investing in next-generation clean diesel, hybrid and battery-electric powertrains, connected vehicle services and new parts distribution centers.

watch.item: PACCAR says changes in tariff policy or emissions rules could affect results; in July 2026 the EPA proposed keeping its 2027 truck nitrogen-oxide limits while revising warranty rules.
If freight conditions weaken with the economy, PACCAR expects more late payments, truck repossessions and credit losses in its finance arm, and less new lending.

companies.name: CME Group Inc.
companies.business: Runs futures and options exchanges and clearing houses (interest rates, stock indexes, energy, farm goods, metals, FX, crypto) and sells market data.
companies.plain: CME Group: trading was a bit slower but sales of market data hit a record; it plans a new service for US government bond trades in December and a new boss next year.

highlights: Net income was $1.04B and profit per share $2.88 ($2.99 adjusted), versus $2.81 ($2.96 adjusted) a year earlier. Clearing and transaction fees were $1.35B, versus $1.39B.
Market data revenue hit a quarterly record of $238.1M, up from $198.1M. Average daily volume was 29.8M contracts, versus 30.2M a year earlier.
CME paid about $468M in dividends and repurchased $695M of stock in the quarter.

guidance.text: The company gives no outlook for the coming period.

next_earnings.note: CME announced on 4 Sep 2026 that it will report Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Wed 21 Oct 2026, with a call at 7:30 a.m. CT.

whats_next.item: CME plans to launch CME Securities Clearing, a new clearing house for US Treasury cash and repo trades, pending regulatory approvals. The SEC requires central clearing of Treasury cash trades by 31 Dec 2026.
Terry Duffy will step down as CEO and become Executive Chairman. President and CFO Lynne Fitzpatrick will become CEO and join the board at that time.
A Sep 2026 filing says Jack Tobin will become Deputy CFO on 2 Nov 2026 and CFO in March 2027, when Fitzpatrick moves to CEO.
In the Q2 release, the CEO named single-stock futures, 1-ounce gold contracts traded 24/7, US Treasury clearing and compute futures as areas of new product work.

watch.item: CME planned compute futures on Nvidia H100 and B200 GPU rental prices for 5 Oct 2026. On 21 Sep the CFTC extended its review by 45 days, to 9 Nov 2026, citing novel or complex issues.
Q2 trading volume and clearing fees were slightly below a year earlier. Revenue growth came mainly from market data, not trading.

companies.name: T-Mobile US, Inc.
companies.business: US wireless carrier (5G mobile phone and data plans) that also sells home broadband and fiber internet through joint ventures.
companies.plain: T-Mobile: service sales keep growing and it now expects more cash this year, but it added fewer new customer accounts; a new finance chief takes over early next year.

highlights: Service revenue rose 8.9% to $19.0B and postpaid service revenue rose 12.6%. T-Mobile's core cash-profit measure (before interest, taxes and depreciation) rose 11.7% to $9.5B.
Postpaid net account additions fell 13% to 277K. Postpaid revenue per account rose 2% to $152.91, and account churn was 0.99% (0.92% a year earlier).
Returned $3.3B to shareholders in Q2 ($2.2B buybacks, $1.1B dividends). Net income was $3.2B (+0.5%) and profit per share was $2.99 (+5.3%).

guidance.text: Raised adjusted free cash flow to $18.4-18.8B and operating cash flow to $28.4-28.8B. Kept its core cash-profit measure at $37.1-37.5B, postpaid net account adds at 950K-1.05M and capital spending at about $10B.

next_earnings.note: Announced by T-Mobile on 17 Sep 2026: results at about 4:05pm ET on Wed 28 Oct 2026, with the call at 4:30pm ET.

whats_next.item: A shareholder return program of up to $18.2B runs through year-end 2026. Another $392M was repurchased in early Q3 (through 17 Jul).
CFO Peter Osvaldik is retiring from the role. Jessica Uhl (former GE Vernova president and former Shell CFO) is CFO-designate and takes over after the 2026 annual report.
whats_next.when: new CFO mid-Sep 2026; current CFO retires Feb 2027

whats_next.item: Closing some dealer and company stores while moving partly to large-format experience stores ($108M of costs in Q2), alongside a 2025-2026 workforce program.

watch.item: Postpaid net account additions slowed to 277K from 318K a year earlier. The full-year target stays at 950K-1.05M.
UScellular merger-related costs ($146M after tax in Q2), severance and store-closing charges held net income growth to 0.5%.

companies.name: Diamondback Energy, Inc.
companies.business: Independent oil and gas producer focused on the Permian Basin in West Texas. It also owns mineral and royalty interests through its Viper Energy subsidiary.
companies.plain: Diamondback Energy: profit more than doubled and it is paying down debt; it expects to pump a bit more oil, but says the oil market is very unpredictable.

highlights: Production averaged 1,018,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day, 525,000 of them oil. The unhedged realized oil price was $96.82 per barrel.
Net income attributable to Diamondback was $1.88B ($6.65 per diluted share), versus $699M ($2.38) a year earlier. Free cash flow was $2.33B.
Total debt fell about $1.3B from the prior quarter to $12.8B. The base dividend was $1.10 per share, and Q2 buybacks totaled about $141M.

guidance.text: Diamondback raised its 2026 guidance to over 522,000 barrels of oil a day and over 1 million barrels of oil equivalent in total, and kept capital spending at about $3.9B. For Q3 it guides to 517,000-527,000 barrels of oil a day and $950M-$1.05B of cash capital spending.

next_earnings.note: Announced 30 Sep 2026: Q3 2026 results come after the market closes on 2 Nov 2026, with a call on 3 Nov at 8:00 a.m. CT.

whats_next.item: The CEO letter says the company dropped its formula-based framework for returning cash and will keep putting excess free cash flow toward cutting debt.
The board doubled the buyback authorization to $16.0B, with about $9.9B left. The company plans to buy back stock opportunistically.
The company added a completion crew to bring forward drilled-but-unfinished wells. It expects its long-haul gas takeaway capacity to more than double by year-end.
The letter describes encouraging early tests in a chemical enhanced-oil-recovery program. It also has a shovel-ready, gigawatt-plus power project, but no signed contract yet.

watch.item: The CEO letter calls the oil market highly volatile and says the timing of supply getting back to normal can't be predicted. It expects cost inflation, for example on casing, into 2027.
On 29-30 Sep 2026, two directors (Darin Holderness and Lance Robertson) resigned in a board stepdown under an amended stockholders agreement with SGF FANG Holdings.

companies.name: Linde plc
companies.business: Supplies industrial gases (oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen and others) to manufacturing, electronics, healthcare and energy customers, and builds gas-processing plants.
companies.plain: Linde: profit grew and its signed future gas-supply deals hit a record after a new electronics contract; legal claims tied to cancelled Russian projects are still open.

highlights: Profit per share was $4.15 (up 11%), or $4.50 adjusted (up 10%). The adjusted operating margin was 29.5%, and underlying sales rose 4%.
Project backlog stands at $11B. The sale-of-gas backlog reached a record $8.1B after a new long-term US electronics supply contract.
Free cash flow was $833M after $1.44B of capital spending. About $1.59B went back to shareholders through dividends and net buybacks.

guidance.text: Linde guides Q3 adjusted profit per share to $4.45-4.55 (up 6-8%) and full-year 2026 to $17.70-17.90 (up 8-9%). It plans $5.5-6.0B of capital spending for 2026.

next_earnings.note: Announced 5 Oct 2026: Q3 2026 results by 06:00 EDT on Thu 29 Oct 2026, with a webcast call at 09:00 EDT.

whats_next.item: Linde plans $5.5-6.0B of capital spending in 2026. It has an $11B project backlog, including a record $8.1B of contracted sale-of-gas projects.
The CEO says customer proposal activity remains robust, mainly in electronics, and expects to grow the backlog further.

watch.item: The 10-Q shows recorded contingent liabilities of $1.1B for terminated RusChemAlliance projects and $0.7B for Amur GPP matters. Claims by Gazprom and RCA are still in court or arbitration.
Guidance for Q3 adjusted profit per share growth of 6-8% is below Q2's 10%. The Q2 reported operating margin was 27.5%, 0.6 points lower than a year earlier.
